name: isolated R script
meaning: An R script run with explicit startup settings rather than silently relying on a prior interactive workspace.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: atomic vector
meaning: A sequence whose elements share one atomic storage type.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: integer literal suffix
meaning: The L suffix requesting integer storage for a suitable R numeric literal.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: recycling
meaning: Repeating a shorter vector’s entries to align an operation with a longer vector, subject to the operation’s rules.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: elementwise logic
meaning: Applying logical operations to corresponding vector positions rather than automatically reducing them to one condition.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: one-based indexing
meaning: Numbering the first element as position one.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: negative subscript
meaning: An R subscript that omits positions rather than selecting them from the end.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: missing logical mask
meaning: An index mask containing an unknown NA entry, which must not silently be treated as FALSE.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: named vector
meaning: A vector with a names attribute that can support character-based selection.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: non-finite value
meaning: A missing, undefined or infinite numeric value that does not pass is.finite.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: NULL versus NA
meaning: The distinction between a length-zero null object and a missing value occupying a vector position.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: string collapse
meaning: Joining several result strings into a single character element using a separator.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: list extraction
meaning: Selecting a sub-list with [ or extracting one component with [[, which are different operations.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: data frame
meaning: A table-like list of columns with a common row count, whose columns may have different types.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: dimension dropping
meaning: Simplifying a subset’s container shape, which can be prevented with an applicable drop=FALSE argument.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: factor code
meaning: An integer encoding of a category according to its factor levels, not necessarily the numeric meaning of its label.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: matrix fill order
meaning: The rule mapping a supplied vector into matrix row and column positions.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: safe index sequence
meaning: An index sequence such as seq_along(x) that correctly becomes empty for zero-length input.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: function default
meaning: An expression supplying a parameter when its argument is omitted, subject to R’s evaluation rules.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: lexical lookup
meaning: Resolving a name through the environment where a function was defined and its enclosing environments.
context: R language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.
